subject: Architecture
title: The Dome of the Rock: Jerusalem's Golden Shrine
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Dome of the Rock: Jerusalem's Golden Shrine.

hook.text: The Dome of the Rock sits on the spot where Muslims believe Muhammad ascended to heaven.

buildup.text: Built in 691 AD, its golden dome and octagonal plan were revolutionary — unlike any previous mosque design.

discovery.text: The shrine protects the Foundation Stone — sacred to Jews as the site of Abraham's sacrifice and Solomon's Temple.

twist.text: The building borrows Byzantine architecture — mosaics, columns, and dome construction — but fills it with Arabic.

climax.text: Its iconic silhouette defines Jerusalem's skyline. Three religions claim the same sacred ground beneath it.

punchline.text: One rock. Three faiths. The most contested ground on Earth.

quiz.question: What does the Dome of the Rock protect?
options: Ancient scrolls from the early Islamic period
The Foundation Stone, sacred to multiple religions
The tomb of a medieval Islamic ruler

details.summary: The Dome of the Rock (completed 691 CE) is one of the oldest surviving Islamic buildings, centered on the Foundation Stone sacred to Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.
details.whyItMatters: The Dome of the Rock demonstrates how architecture asserts religious and political authority over contested sacred ground. It was designed to surpass Jerusalem's Christian churches visually.
takeaways: Completed 691 CE, one of the oldest surviving Islamic buildings
Built over the Foundation Stone sacred to three religions
Designed to visually surpass Jerusalem's Christian churches

faq.question: Is the Dome of the Rock a mosque?
faq.answer: Not exactly. It is a shrine, not a congregational mosque. Muslims pray at the nearby Al-Aqsa Mosque. The Dome of the Rock was built to enshrine the sacred rock from which Muhammad is believed to have ascended to heaven. Its purpose is commemoration and pilgrimage rather than daily worship.

faq.question: Is the dome actually made of gold?
faq.answer: The current dome is covered in gold leaf applied over aluminum panels during a 1993 restoration funded by King Hussein of Jordan, who sold one of his London houses to pay for it. Earlier coverings were copper and lead. The original 7th-century dome was likely gilded as well.
